correctness.rationale: Definition 5 arrow-to-target update is used, not world-deletion. With alternating size-two S5 equivalence blocks, the remaining active targets after k rounds are exactly {0,...,n-k-1}; the unique relevant opposite-p witness of each active j<n-1 is j+1, while n-1 has none. Hence exactly n strict updates. In any one-agent S5 block, all worlds of one valuation type share all modal truths; a strict round removes at least one type, and a quiescent block never restarts. At most min(n,2^r) global rounds; the universal-block chain of m distinct Boolean types and formula OR(q_j AND diamond q_{j+1}) attains m. No claim about world-deleting PAL or continued S5 after arrow deletions.
residual_risks: Finite n simulation corroborates but does not establish all-size theorem; the induction and type deletion do.
